title: Rusalka – free piano app: learn any song from a photo of the sheet music
description: Learn piano with any song you like. Take a photo of the sheet music, any AI chat turns it into a song for Rusalka, and Rusalka shows the next key, waits for you and plays along. Free, in the browser, no account.
ogTitle: Rusalka – learn piano with any song you like
ogDescription: A photo of the sheet music, any AI chat, and the song is ready to play. Free piano app in the browser for children and beginners.
h1: Learn piano with any song you like
lead: Take a photo of the sheet music and the AI chat you already use turns it into a song for Rusalka. Rusalka then shows which key comes next, waits until you find it and plays along. Free, in the browser, for children and beginners.
small: Free. No account, no ads. Works offline after the first visit.
playAria: The same song in Rusalka: coloured notes with letters and lyrics, the next key lights up on the keyboard
playLabel: The same song, ready to play in Rusalka
aiH2: From a picture to a song in three steps
ai1: In Rusalka, open AI and copy the instructions.
ai2: Paste them into ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or another AI chat, with a photo of the notes.
ai3: Paste the answer back into Rusalka. The song is in your list, ready to play.
aiAria: Recording: copying the instructions from Rusalka, the AI chat writes out the song from a picture of sheet music, pasting it back
whyH2: The song your child wants, not the one in the app
whyLead: Most piano apps teach from their own catalogue. With Rusalka you start from the music you have: a songbook at home, a page from a music lesson, or a song you found online.
why1p: A photo from a songbook, a scan, a PDF or a screenshot. The AI chat writes out the melody, the chords and the lyrics.
why2h: The AI chat you already have
why2p: Rusalka gives you the instructions to copy, so any AI chat knows exactly what to write. Rusalka itself sends nothing anywhere.
why3p: The AI chat can also write an easier version of a song: fewer notes, five fingers, a simpler left hand.
why4p: The song opens in an editor that checks every bar and shows the notes, so you can fix a misread note before you play.
noAi: No AI? Rusalka also opens MusicXML and MIDI files, and its library has children’s songs, folk songs, Christmas carols and classical pieces ready to play.
stepsLead: Every song is learned in the same three steps. Notes can show letters and colours, so even a child who cannot read music yet can play.
step1p: Rusalka waits for the right key. No tempo, no hurry.
step2p: Rusalka plays the accompaniment and still waits for you.
step3p: Now you keep the tempo yourself.
resultAlt: Result screen: three stars, Bravo!, all notes played, the bar with the most mistakes
starsP: After each attempt you get up to three stars and one sentence about what to practise: the bar with the most mistakes and what went wrong there. Children can also listen back to how it sounded.
familyLead: Each player can choose an animal and a colour for their profile and keep track of their own progress.
playersAlt: Who is playing? Three players: Ela with a rabbit, Tom with a piano, Mia with a fox
statsAlt: Statistics: progress in four songs and where it gets stuck, with a Practise button for each bar
statsCaption: Statistics show which songs are learned and where it gets stuck, with a button to practise just that bar.
family1: Two children at one piano: one plays the melody, the other the bass.
family2: Letters or colours on the notes, finger numbers, an easier key.
family3: A loop for a hard passage that speeds up a little each time.
need1p: A computer or tablet with Chrome or Edge and a digital piano connected by a USB cable or Bluetooth (MIDI).
need2p: Play the keys on the screen, or an ordinary piano that Rusalka hears through the microphone.
need3p: Safari cannot use a MIDI piano. A computer (Mac or PC) with Chrome or Edge works best, and saving to a folder works there too. On an iPad you can try the free {webmidi} app, but Rusalka hasn't been tested in it.
need4p: Open {app} and play. You can add it to your home screen or dock as an app.
faq1p: Yes. No subscription, no ads and nothing to buy inside.
faq2p: No. Songs, players and results stay in your browser and Rusalka sends them nowhere. You can download a backup, or keep everything in a folder on your computer.
faq3h: Does it work without the internet?
faq3p: Yes. After the first visit the browser keeps everything it needs.
faq5p: Any sheet music you may use: folk songs, music in the public domain, openly licensed scores or sheet music you bought. Your songs stay on your device.
faq6p: A dad of two children who wanted to play their favourite songs on the piano but could not read music reliably yet. The children were the testers.
endP: Pick a song from the library and start playing.
